draft.title: Rust Host and CLI, a strict TypeScript workbench, and no Electron client
constraints: Rust owns the Host, native runtime, CLI, supervision and first-party coordination
the workbench is strict TypeScript, preferably React, compiled to static assets
no Electron client and no second Go core language
alternatives: Electron, excluded by explicit client constraint
Go as a second core language, excluded by explicit client constraint
consequences: language-specific SDK and analyzer sidecars stay sidecars behind versioned protocols
desktop remains a Host client without canonical state or headless work lifetime
draft.security: the client shell holds no canonical state or Host authority; Preview content, localhost included, is untrusted and needs an isolated permission surface and a narrow authenticated design bridge
draft.reversal: replacing the language stack after dependent implementation would rewrite the Host and the client; the client accepted that cost by instruction rather than by measurement

evidence.method: the client's execution takeover instruction as recorded 2026-09-08 UTC; this check verifies these bytes and does not fetch or authenticate them
evidence.reviewer: client instruction; no independent reviewer of these records exists in this repository

acceptance.client_exception: the client fixed the Host language and excluded Electron by instruction rather than by benchmark, so this acceptance rests on that authority and not on measured evidence

draft.title: Desktop shell: Tauri 2 is the preferred, unproven candidate and Electron is ineligible
constraints: no shell implementation may treat Tauri 2 as the final choice before #38 records its measurements
Preview origins, localhost included, inherit neither workbench nor Host authority
a failed hard requirement triggers a documented non-Electron alternative, never reduced Preview scope
alternatives: Electron, excluded by explicit client constraint
any non-Electron shell that passes the representative workload
consequences: dependent shell implementation stops on an unresolved hard requirement
shell, packaging and cross-platform behavior stay unproven until the proof artifacts exist
draft.security: Preview is untrusted; an iframe is not the boundary, and the design surface needs isolated permissions and a narrow authenticated bridge
draft.reversal: a shell is not chosen by preference: acceptance needs measured evidence or an explicit client exception, and replacing one later needs its own migration and rollback evidence

draft.title: System Graph storage: SurrealDB is the preferred, unproven candidate
constraints: verify actual version, behavior, resource profile and deployment model before implementing
control-plane transactional persistence is evaluated separately from System Graph storage
no storage implementation may treat the candidate as final before its proof
alternatives: another graph, vector and full-text store that meets the measured requirements
separate persistence for the control plane
consequences: System Graph implementation waits on the storage proof
storage stays behind explicit protocols to bound migration cost
draft.security: stored knowledge carries provenance and uncertainty rather than presenting inferred knowledge as confirmed
draft.reversal: storage is chosen on measured version, behavior, resource and deployment evidence, so acceptance needs that evidence or an explicit client exception; this record performs no state migration
